page.notes: The first note line is "Duplicia in-/genia apud Ariftot.", set in two lines and beside the first lines of the paragraph; the second note "Quinq; ingeniorum classes." stands beside the line "hæc sanè capita". The note "1." and "Ingenia nimis mobilia." are in the left margin beside the paragraph "I. Sunt ingenia". The Greek words in the paragraph "I. Sunt ingenia" are uncertain in their exact letters and accents, especially the second Greek word of the pair after "Græci" and the last word before "dixerunt"; they are marked [?]. The verse line "Qui sapit ante pilos" is set without indent and is a line of verse. The word after "debet" is printed as a hyphenated "su-" with "um" on the next line; the first letter is doubtful (long s in italic-like type), so it is marked as suum with the hyphen as printed. The catchword "2.Inge-" is read from its position at the lower right. The first paragraph continues from the previous page.
